subject: Thomas Brooks Park Archaeological Preservation Plan
overview: The commission found a fire-damaged property not significant, accepted a new demolition application, and discussed interpretive designs for the Thomas Brooks Park archaeological site. Members also finalized 2024 organizational matters and received updates on burial ground research.

items.title: 43 Austin Street Significance Determination
items.summary: Found the property not historically significant due to extensive fire damage and a lack of unique architectural or social history, allowing the demolition process to proceed.

items.title: 3.14 Winthrop Street Application Acceptance
items.summary: Accepted the demolition application as complete and scheduled a significance determination for the February meeting.

items.title: Thomas Brooks Park Preservation Design
items.summary: Reviewed a conceptual design presentation for the archaeological site, with commissioners favoring foundation tracing, ADA-accessible paths, and interpretive signage covering indigenous and colonial history. Landscape architect Peter Handland will synthesize the feedback into more detailed concept plans for future funding requests.

items.title: Annual Report and 2024 Organization
items.summary: Approved the annual report, confirmed the 2024 slate of officers and meeting schedule, and established subcommittees for survey planning and demolition delay process review.

items.title: Section 106 Review: I-93 Bridge Repairs
items.summary: Decided to offer no comment on proposed MassDOT repairs for ten bridges along Interstate 93, noting they are not historic in a traditional sense.

items.title: Cemetery and Survey Updates
items.summary: Received an update on the Cross Street Burial Ground, where archaeological testing is recommended to locate intact burials before any potential site development. The commission also reviewed the progress of ongoing historical surveys in the Fulton Heights and Hall Estate neighborhoods.
